title: PM-friendly SDK 30min quickstart and demo checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, PM-focused quickstart and demo checklist for giving a 25–30 minute walkthrough of the Redwood SDK to non-engineering stakeholders (PMs, design, bizdev). The goal is to enable a convincing proto/POC in a single short session: install, call, inspect telemetry, and iterate prompts.

Tone and constraints:
- Non-technical friendly: emphasize copy, screenshots, expected outcomes, and failure-mode scripts.
- Minimal setup: avoid infra (no Dedicated or Private setup) — use hosted sandbox token.
- Repro path: curl + Node snippet + one browser-based playground (playground link included).

TL;DR 30-minute plan (timeboxed):
0:00–02:00 — Quick framing (why SDK matters for your product; 2 slides max).
02:00–05:00 — Prereqs & safety check (token, sandbox link, local terminal).
05:00–12:00 — Live: curl example hitting text-generation endpoint, show streaming.
12:00–18:00 — Swap to small Node script showing structured output + function call.
18:00–22:00 — Open Redwood Console telemetry: tokens, latency, example traces.
22:00–27:00 — Tweak prompt and show immediate diff in console (cost/latency/quality).
27:00–30:00 — Next steps, ask for their success criteria, and schedule follow-up POC.

Prerequisites for demonstrator (what to prep):
- Sandbox API key (limited quota) saved in a short URL (we use pw-protected notes).
- Local laptop with curl and Node installed.
- Browser tab open to sandbox playground: https://playground.redwood.ai/sandbox (example link).
- Example dataset (3 sample user messages) in a Gist for reuse.
- Small readout slide with three success metrics: latency (<200ms), cost per 1k tokens, hallucination tolerance.

Quickstart artifacts to have on-hand (copyable):
1) Email invite blurb (one paragraph):
"Join a 30-minute walkthrough where we ship a tiny LLM feature from zero to demo. We'll: run a live SDK call, inspect cost/latency in Console, and iterate prompts so you can define success criteria. No infra needed — bring a laptop and a browser."

2) One-line curl (copy-paste):
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <SANDBOX_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize the user message in one sentence"}'

3) Minimal Node example (paste into a file demo.js):
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async()=>{
  const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',{
    method:'POST',
    headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+process.env.RW_KEY,'Content-Type':'application/json'},
    body:JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-small-1',input:'Rewrite: I need help booking flights'})
  });
  const json = await resp.json();
  console.log('result:', json.output_text || json.choices?.[0]?.text);
})();

4) In-browser playground script: payload snippet users can paste into the UI (short copy).

Guided demo script (narration + actions):
- "We’ll keep it tiny: three calls total. First, a plain summary to show basic output. Second, structure the output (JSON) for product UI ease. Third, tweak prompt to reduce hallucination."
- Action: paste curl -> show response -> paste Node -> run -> show Console entry in telemetry.

Telemetry & Console checks to show (quick wins):
- Token breakdown for the request: prompt tokens vs generated tokens.
- Per-route latency and p50/p95 visible for the demo window.
- Trace view: correlate request id to model variant and region.
- Cost estimate widget: show how a 10k user cohort translates to monthly spend.

Prompt iteration mini-loop (fast heuristic):
1) Baseline prompt (short).
2) Add a one-line "output format" instruction (JSON schema) to reduce parsing work.
3) Add a guard clause: "If you are uncertain, say 'unknown' rather than inventing facts.'"
4) Re-run and compare quality / tokens.

Failure-mode scripts (what to say when things go wrong):
- If network/curl fails: "Let's switch to the playground and re-run — same payload."
- If token limit exceeded: "We’ll trim the prompt and re-run; also I’ll open the Console to adjust batch settings for next run."
- If output is hallucinating: "We’ll add a strict schema and a knowledge cutoff line, then re-evaluate."

PM-centric acceptance checklist (post-demo):
- Did we show an end-to-end happy path (input -> structured output -> telemetry trace)? (Y/N)
- Is the latency within the expected interactive range for your product? (record p50)
- Does the structured output map to your UI data model? (attach sample mapping)
- Can we define a one-week POC objective with measurable KPIs? (assign owner + date)

Copy snippets for product copy / user-facing microcopy:
- Empty state microcopy for an LLM feature: "Ask me anything about your orders — I’ll summarize and point you to details."
- Error fallback microcopy: "Hmm, I can't find a confident answer right now. Try rephrasing or check back in a few seconds."

Safety and compliance quick notes for PMs (one-liners):
- Use sandbox keys for demos (never production keys).
- PII: strip or tokenize any sensitive data in the demo.
- Audit logs: show Console’s request history for basic auditability.

Post-demo followup templates:
- Immediate follow-up email to attendees (copy):
  "Thanks — attaching the demo artifacts, curl + node snippets, and a 3-step plan to get an internal POC started. If you want, we can run a focused 60-minute POC next week with your sample dataset."

Open questions / TODOs (for DX team):
- Create a single-click sandbox key generator for recurring demos (RDW-421 ticket).
- Shorten the Node example to a one-liner for macOS default shells.
- Add a "PM mode" in the Console that highlights the 3 telemetry cards referenced above.

Notes-to-self (demo-time hacks):
- Keep a second browser profile with a prelogged Console for fast switches.
- If streaming stalls, reload the playground and show a cached prior request.
- Have a screenshot of an ideal Console trace ready to paste into Slack during the meeting.

References and quick links:
- Sandbox playground: https://playground.redwood.ai/sandbox
- SDK repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/782
- Internal ticket: RDW-421

Bottom line: this doc should survive as a one-page kit you can hand to any PM and they can run a convincing demo in 30 minutes. Keep it opinionated, and keep the friction to "open terminal -> paste -> run".
